description: ICS Village at DEF CON 26 covers Industrial Control Systems security and critical infrastructure protection. The talks explore ICS/IoT defense mechanisms, firmware security, side-channel attacks, VPN vulnerabilities, behavioral defense systems, and practical security training for industrial environments.

talks.title: A SOC in the Sandbox
talks.summary:
### Operational Realities of Industrial Control Security
At 00:00, Tom VanNorman, Director of Engineering Services at Dragos, discusses designing and staffing Security Operations Centers (SOCs) specifically tailored for industrial control systems (ICS/SCADA) at the ICS Village. VanNorman addresses common pitfalls when enterprise IT teams attempt to manage operational technology (OT) environments.

### The Headcount and Technology Silver-Bullet Fallacy
At 03:14, VanNorman challenges common corporate misconceptions, explaining that merely increasing headcount or purchasing general IT security tools will not secure an industrial plant. Because OT environments rely on proprietary industrial networks, successful monitoring requires specialized domain knowledge of physical processes and automation systems.

### Developing Repeatable OT Incident Response Playbooks
At 06:40, the presentation emphasizes standardized operational procedures. VanNorman highlights that in ICS environments, operational availability, employee safety, and equipment integrity take precedence over data confidentiality, requiring customized triage workflows that prevent security controls from inadvertently causing plant shutdowns.

### Unified Telemetry and Industrial Network Visibility
Concluding between 09:52 and 13:02, VanNorman reviews technical architectures for ICS visibility. He stresses the necessity of passive network monitoring across specialized industrial protocols (such as Modbus, DNP3, and Ethernet/IP) to detect unauthorized controller logic changes and firmware modifications without injecting active network traffic.

talks.title: How can industrial IoT be protected
talks.teaser: How can industrial IoT be protected
talks.summary:
### Security Challenges in the Industrial Internet of Things
At 00:00, industrial cybersecurity researchers Keiser and Barenz examine defense methodologies for safeguarding Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensors, actuators, and supervisory control systems within critical infrastructure.

### The Vulnerability of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs)
At 04:01, the presenters explain the architectural constraints of industrial control hardware. Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and field sensors operate on low-power, deterministic microcontrollers that cannot support endpoint detection agents, memory protections, or complex cryptographic handshakes without introducing dangerous cycle delays into physical processes.

### The Flaws of Monolithic Enterprise VPNs in ICS
At 08:00, the speakers critique traditional remote access models. Connecting remote technicians to operational technology (OT) networks using standard corporate VPNs creates flat, routable network bridges that allow malware on external laptops to pivot directly into sensitive controller networks.

### Hardware-Enforced Secure Tunnels and Micro-Segmentation
At 12:02 and 16:03, Keiser and Barenz demonstrate a hardware-enforced secure tunneling architecture. Utilizing cryptographic USB iKeys containing pre-configured tunnel definitions, the system establishes point-to-point encrypted connections directly between authorized technicians and specific field endpoints, avoiding routable enterprise network exposure.

### Agnostic Field Deployment and Resource Efficiency
Concluding at 20:00, the authors present live demonstration results from the ICS Village capture-the-flag arena. They illustrate that hardware-agnostic, micro-segmented tunneling drastically reduces configuration overhead and administrative human error while insulating sensitive industrial controllers from broader enterprise threats.

talks.title: Behavior Based Defense in ICS Environments
talks.teaser: Behavior Based Defense in ICS Environments
talks.summary:
### The Evolution of ICS Threat Landscapes
At 00:00, adversary hunter and industrial cybersecurity researcher Joe Slowik examines behavior-based defense strategies for securing critical infrastructure at the ICS Village. Slowik outlines how targeted OT threats have matured beyond opportunistic malware toward highly capable nation-state campaigns.

### Moving Beyond Signatures and Indicators of Compromise
At 08:58, Slowik discusses the fundamental limitations of static indicators of compromise (IOCs) such as file hashes and known IP addresses. Sophisticated adversaries rapidly mutate their tooling and leverage living-off-the-land techniques, rendering traditional perimeter signature defenses largely ineffective in critical environments.

### Identifying Adversary Lateral Movement and Credential Access
At 17:52, the presentation analyzes adversary behavior within converged IT/OT networks. Slowik illustrates how attackers abuse administrative tools, PowerShell scripts, WMI routines, and credential harvesting utilities like Mimikatz across intermediate jump hosts before attempting to bridge into operational control networks.

### Industrial Protocol Anomaly Detection and Process Disruption
Concluding between 26:23 and 35:00, Slowik details how defenders can identify malicious intent at the process level. By monitoring engineering command structures, uncharacteristic polling behaviors, and unauthorized PLC reprogramming sequences, defenders can disrupt attacks before adversaries induce physical equipment damage or service outages.

talks.title: TOR for The IOT aka TORT Reform
talks.teaser: TOR for The IOT aka TORT Reform
talks.summary:
### The Structural Vulnerability of Consumer IoT
At 00:00, Bryson Bort (founder of SCYTHE and GRIMM) presents an incisive critique of consumer Internet of Things (IoT) security, questioning the reckless connectivity embedded into modern household appliances.

### The Problem of Unnecessary Appliance Connectivity
At 06:01, Bort challenges foundational industry assumptions, humorously questioning why everyday home items like toasters, blenders, and light fixtures require persistent internet connections and remote cloud management when their primary functions are entirely local.

### Consumer Usability vs. Enterprise Security Controls
At 12:01, the speaker analyzes consumer market dynamics. Homeowners prioritize frictionless plug-and-play setup over complex configuration. Consequently, manufacturers ship smart devices with unauthenticated management interfaces, open UPnP ports, and static default passwords to minimize customer service calls.

### Weaponizing Smart Homes into Botnets
At 18:01 and 24:00, Bort demonstrates the consequences of unhardened IoT deployments. Threat actors exploit automated credential scanning and known CVEs to compromise millions of household devices, converting innocuous cameras and smart appliances into weaponized DDoS botnet infrastructure (such as Mirai) or stealthy network pivot points into home office systems.

### TORT Reform: Local Containment and Micro-Segmentation
Concluding the session, Bort proposes "TORT Reform"—a set of pragmatic architectural remedies including strict IoT network micro-segmentation, default-deny outbound firewall rules, and vendor accountability to ensure smart devices cannot compromise wider network perimeters.

talks.title: A CTF That Teaches
talks.summary:
### Designing Educational Capture The Flag Competitions for ICS
At 00:00, Brandon Workentin from SecurityMatters presents on the architectural and educational principles behind designing effective industrial control system Capture The Flag (CTF) challenges at the ICS Village. Workentin explores how gamified challenges can bridge the technical knowledge gap between IT and OT engineers.

### The Divergence Between Traditional IT and Industrial Systems
At 07:02, Workentin explains the unique technical hurdles faced by traditional web and binary CTF players when encountering industrial control systems. Unlike standard Windows or Linux targets, industrial hardware utilizes real-time operating systems (RTOS), ladder logic programs, and proprietary industrial communication buses.

### Emulating Authentic Physical Infrastructure
At 14:24, the presentation explores the physical hardware engineering behind the competition. Workentin demonstrates how organizers integrated real-world programmable logic controllers (PLCs), human-machine interfaces (HMIs), and ruggedized field PCs into hands-on challenge benches that authentically simulate municipal water treatment and power distribution environments.

### Scaffolded Learning and Competency Progression
Concluding between 21:08 and 26:00, Workentin outlines instructional scaffolding methods. He emphasizes designing multi-tiered challenge tracks that first teach foundational industrial packet capture and protocol parsing before escalating to advanced firmware reverse engineering and physical process manipulation.
